definitions.explanation: A person or shop that makes or alters clothing to fit individual customers. Can refer to either the craftsperson or the establishment.

examples.japanese: {仕立屋|したてや}にスーツを{頼|たの}んだ。
examples.english: I ordered a suit from the tailor.

examples.japanese: この{町|まち}には{腕|うで}のいい{仕立屋|したてや}がある。
examples.english: There's a skilled tailor in this town.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}、{仕立屋|したてや}で{着物|きもの}の{仕立|した}てを{習|なら}った。
examples.english: My grandmother learned kimono tailoring at a tailor's shop when she was young.

notes:
A traditional occupation word formed from {仕立|した}て (tailoring, sewing) + {屋|や} (shop/person). While dedicated tailor shops have become less common in modern Japan, the word is still used and understood.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仕立屋|したてや}に{出|だ}す: to send to the tailor
- {仕立屋|したてや}に{頼|たの}む: to commission a tailor
- {腕|うで}のいい{仕立屋|したてや}: a skilled tailor

RELATED WORDS:
- {仕立|した}てる: to tailor; to sew — the verb form
- オーダーメイド: custom-made — the modern loanword alternative
- {洋裁|ようさい}: Western dressmaking
- {和裁|わさい}: Japanese garment making
